import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_5/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_5/training_1.csv"

df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History: JOIN on ["city", "city"] between Source2_5_0 and Source2_5_1
# Join df_source0 and df_source1 on 'city' column (inner join by default)
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Target schema: ['city': string, 'ride_id': integer]
# Extract only the required columns for the target table
df_target = df_joined[["city", "ride_id"]].copy()

# Ensure correct data types
df_target["city"] = df_target["city"].astype(str)
df_target["ride_id"] = df_target["ride_id"].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_5/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 as instructed
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_5/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_5/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# The target schema is ['city', 'ride_id'] with 'city' as key and 'ride_id' integer
# The join produces multiple ride_id per city, but target has unique city keys
# So we group by city and aggregate ride_id by taking the minimum (or any deterministic aggregation)
result = joined.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({"ride_id": "min"})

# Write output with exact column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_5/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
